'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali war]]
**The village of [[Tidermène]] is captured by the [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara]]. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2023/04/12/is-jihadists-tidermene-mali/ (Defense Post)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[NPR]] announces that it will no longer use [[Twitter]] after the social media site labeled it and the [[BBC]] as "government-funded media". Shortly thereafter, Twitter CEO [[Elon Musk]] announces that the labelling of the BBC will be changed to "publicly-funded media". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-65202978 (BBC News)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/04/12/npr-is-first-major-us-news-outlet-to-stop-using-twitter.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty-five people are killed and others are missing after a [[List of migrant vessel incidents on the Mediterranean Sea|boat carrying migrants sinks]] off the coast of [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/12/ten-refugees-from-sub-saharan-africa-drown-off-coast-of-tunisia (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Saudi Arabia–Syria relations]]
**Syrian foreign minister [[Faisal Mekdad]] meets with [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia)|Saudi foreign minister]] [[Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud|Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud]] in [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]], in the first such visit between the two countries since the start of the [[Syrian civil war]] in 2011 in order to discuss the security situation in [[Syria]] and the return of [[Refugees of the Syrian civil war|Syrian refugees]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/12/syrian-fm-makes-first-visit-to-saudi-arabia-since-2011 (Al Jazeera)]
